summary: Phase 9C+9D testing. Found CRITICAL frontend regression that crashed all chats; fixed it. NewGroupDialog single-step works. Backend has a subtle but real bug in _has_perm() where missing keys in a partial admin_permissions map default to True (granting unset perms). Frontend EditRoleModal currently sends all 6 perms so this latent bug is masked end-to-end, but it WILL surface for any future caller (mobile/API) that sends a partial perms payload. PATCH /api/groups/{id}/admins/{user_id} works for owner; PATCH endpoint authorization for non-owner relies on the same _has_perm logic and inherits this bug.

critical.issue: Returns bool(perms.get(perm, True)) — when an admin's admin_permissions map is set but does NOT contain a specific perm key, that perm is granted by default. Means PATCHing {permissions:{can_pin:true}} actually grants the admin ALL six perms because the other five keys default to True. Reproduce: PATCH /api/groups/<id>/admins/<bob> body={'permissions':{'can_pin':true}}; then as bob POST /api/groups/<id>/ban/<x> -> returns 200 (should be 403). Should be: when perms map exists and is non-empty, missing keys must default to FALSE; only when the entire entry is absent should the admin inherit ALL (backward compat).

minor.issue: Title >16 chars returns 422 via Pydantic max_length validation. Spec wording 'max 16 chars' could be either truncate or reject — current reject behavior is reasonable but frontend should mirror with maxLength=16 on input (already does).

ui_bugs.issue: REGRESSION: Phase 9C added selectionMode/isSelected/onToggleSelect/onEnterSelection prop references at lines 222-224 and the long-press handler, but the function-component prop destructuring (line 95-108) did NOT include them. This caused 'ReferenceError: selectionMode is not defined' inside every MessageBubble render, instantly crashing the entire chat panel for any conversation with messages (caught by error boundary, replaced chat with white screen). I APPLIED the minimal fix: added the four props to destructuring and wired useLongPress to call onEnterSelection when provided. Verified page errors dropped from 1 -> 0 on reload.

integration_issues.issue: After the MessageBubble fix the chat no longer crashes and composer is reachable, but my Playwright bubble locators using .filter(has_text=...) on '[data-testid^=message-bubble-]' did not match freshly-sent text bubbles within the 30s window — likely because the text node sits in a descendant element. NEEDS RE-RUN by main agent with a more specific selector (e.g. last bubble or testid suffixed with msg id from network response). I did NOT validate the actual Copy/Delete/Forward outcomes end-to-end due to this selector issue.

critical_code_review_comments: MessageBubble.jsx: missing props in destructuring is a textbook regression that would've been caught by a single render test. Suggest adding a smoke unit test that mounts MessageBubble with minimal props.

_has_perm in server.py: the 'inherit ALL on missing entry' semantics are correct but the per-key default should be FALSE once any entry exists. Current code mixes both into one default and is semantically wrong.
ChatPanel.jsx is 1869 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting multi-select toolbar, multi-delete modal, and forward orchestration into separate components.
MessageBubble.jsx is 484 lines and growing; the prop list is also growing. A typed props contract (TS or PropTypes) would prevent the destructuring drift that caused this regression.

rca_of_the_issue: Frontend crash: Phase 9C wiring added new prop usages without updating the destructuring signature. ESLint did not flag because react components destructure dynamically. Fixed by adding the 4 missing props to the function signature and switching long-press to call onEnterSelection. Backend _has_perm: original author chose `.get(perm, True)` intending backward-compat, but `if not perms: return True` already handles that — the default in the explicit-map branch should be False.
